title: Lineage VI foundational body plan
scope: Foundational body plan of Lineage VI, the segmented exoskeletal radiation, including growth mode as a branch-level axis and its ancestral state. Species, names, taxonomy, segment and limb counts, sizes, upper size limits, branch inventory, skeleton composition, growth mechanics, large-body physiological support, reproduction, development, sociality, Mana patterns, and local presence remain open.
approval_evidence: After the growth-mode cards were presented, the Author directed that all three modes be retained as branches within the lineage and that some members exceed Earth arthropod sizes; the revised three-branch model was presented with an ancestry question, and the Author selected 'A — Moult ancestral' on 2026-08-17.
question: What is Lineage VI's bounded foundational body plan, how does its exoskeleton grow, and which growth mode is ancestral?
selection: Segmented jointed-exoskeleton lineage, the planet's most species-rich macroscopic animal radiation, mostly small-bodied, with independent small-scale flight in some branches and pollinator-analogue, litter and soil, parasitic, scavenging, predatory, and swarm-prey roles. Skeletal growth is a branch-level axis with three modes: moult branches shed the whole skeleton and pass through a soft vulnerable phase, may undergo life-stage transformation, and stay small; seam-growth branches never shed and expand continuously at flexible inter-plate seams without a soft phase or transformation; rolling-replacement branches shed and regrow plates individually and are never wholly soft. Whole-body moulting is ancestral, with the other two modes derived escapes, and seam-growth branches include large-bodied members exceeding Earth arthropod sizes.
alternatives: L6-GROWTH-A: moult ancestral with seam growth and rolling replacement derived; selected for ancestry.
L6-GROWTH-B: seam growth ancestral with moulting derived; not selected (makes large size ancestral and ordinary).
L6-GROWTH-C: rolling replacement ancestral; not selected (least intuitive ancestor, middling explanatory value).
Single-mode lineage: the original card structure choosing one growth mode for the whole lineage; superseded by the Author's direction to retain all three as branches.
rationale: Retaining all three modes as branches turns growth mode into an axis that predicts the kind of animal, giving one lineage three internally coherent branch families. Moult-ancestral ordering reads as constraint-then-escape: small moulting forms remain the abundant everyday default, each derived mode's advantage is explicit, and the lineage's large-bodied members become an earned innovation of the seam-growth branches rather than an unexplained baseline.
evidence: Author structural direction and selection on 2026-08-17.
consequences: Lineage VI contains three growth-mode branch families rather than one lineage-wide rule.
Small moulting forms are the abundant everyday default of the biosphere.
Seam-growth branches include large-bodied members exceeding Earth arthropod sizes.
Each growth mode carries distinct costs: periodic defencelessness, seam weakness and feeding dependence, or permanently fresh weak plates.
Larger-than-Earth body sizes require respiratory, circulatory, and structural support that remains open and binding.
Later Lineage VI branch and species development must build on this plan.
No Earth homology, particular large creature, or System mechanic is created.
residual_unknowns: Species, names, taxonomy, segment counts, limb counts, sizes, and branch inventory remain open.
Skeleton composition, seam mechanics, moult mechanics, repair, and mineral requirements remain open.
The respiratory, circulatory, and structural support permitting larger-than-Earth body sizes remains open.
Upper size limits and whether any large branch is flight-capable remain open.
Reproduction, egg or brood form, development, life-stage transformation detail, and lifespan remain open.
Sociality, swarming, parasitic strategies, Mana patterns, and local presence remain open.
reopening_conditions: The three-branch growth-mode structure proves unworkable.
Large-bodied branches cannot be supported physiologically.
A concrete contradiction with an accepted or provisional record emerges.
The Author explicitly reopens the decision.
